Title: Patrologiae graecae tomus CLV: Symeon Thessalonicensis archiepiscopus. Symeonis Thessalonicensis archiepiscopi Opera omnia, Jassii in Moldavia anno 1683 Graece; Latine vero nunc primum edita. Tomus unicus
Creator: Symeon, archbishop of Thessalonica (the volume heads him 'Saeculum XV, annus 1430'); Greek text of the Jassy edition of 1683 with Latin by the Migne editors, edited by J.-P. Migne
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne (Petit-Montrouge), Patrologiae cursus completus, Series graeca, tomus 155
Publication Date: 1866
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads '1866' twice in this scan's OCR (file lines 172 and 227); the list of Migne's volumes in tomus CLXI (file line 110919 of the Bessarion volume) reads 'CLV (1866)'. Host record: date field 1857, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item patrologicursus107migngoog (archive.org/details/patrologicursus107migngoog), full-text file patrologicursus107migngoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The file is 3637036 bytes, 2577477 characters and 71743 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 3587, 35871 and 68155): Greek polytonic readable with chi for kappa slips; Latin clean.
Content note: Symeon of Thessalonica's works: the dialogue against all heresies, the treatises on the sacred rites and on the holy temple, on prayer and the sacraments, and his letters and responses, as listed in the volume's ELENCHUS. He was an archbishop of Thessalonica, the see Palamas held. The Greek is from a 1683 Moldavian printing; the Latin is Migne's first translation.
